stories.title: Kiosk GPU-raster fix -- drop --enable-gpu-rasterization to kill the freeze class
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #1 -- CORRECTED PREMISE 2026-08-02, design-gate] --enable-gpu-rasterization is NOT in the repo or the eclipse-dashboard unit; it is a Debian/RPi-OS system default injected by the /usr/bin/chromium-browser wrapper from /etc/chromium.d/default-flags:7. FIX = ADD an override flag to the eclipse-dashboard unit ExecStart (deploy-pi.sh, repo-managed): --disable-gpu-rasterization (keep GL compositing) OR --disable-gpu (bulletproof software render, removes the whole GPU-command-buffer path). Atlas leans --disable-gpu (the Pi CPU trivially handles this 2D card UI; removes the entire failure class). Eliminates the chromium GPU command-buffer hot-loop (AllocateRingBuffer kFatalFailure, ~6M/boot) that froze the UI. RCA: offices/architect/findings/2026-08-02-pi-ui-freeze-chromium-gpu-command-buffer-hotloop.md

[PRECEDENCE -- verify, do NOT assume] the Debian wrapper runs `chromium $CHROMIUM_FLAGS "$@"`, so the ExecStart override SHOULD win over the injected default -- but VERIFY on the Pi (a wrapper-ordering surprise = silent mocked-green / IRL-miss)

[A-16 deploy-contract blind spot] chromium's base flags live in an OS-shipped /etc/chromium.d/ file the repo does not manage; add a one-line comment in deploy-pi.sh so a future chromium package upgrade re-introducing GPU raster is a known surface
installs via the existing cmp-guarded kiosk-unit step + daemon-reload; ruff/lint clean in-loop

validationCriteria.action: post-deploy on the Pi, `pgrep -a chromium` to confirm the override wins over /etc/chromium.d, then sustained carousel navigation for several minutes + `journalctl -u eclipse-dashboard | grep -c AllocateRingBuffer`
validationCriteria.outcome: the RUNNING chromium cmdline shows GPU rasterization effectively off (override present + winning), AllocateRingBuffer count stays ~0, chromium CPU low, display never freezes

conditionalOutcomes: if the ExecStart override does NOT win over /etc/chromium.d/default-flags (wrapper-ordering surprise), STOP and escalate to Atlas -- do not assume precedence
if GPU-off alone does NOT eliminate the freeze, escalate -- fix-selection (disable-gpu vs disable-gpu-rasterization vs cma vs animations) is a hypothesis; do not stack blind changes
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the Pi dashboard to never freeze under sustained use, so the display stays live during a drive instead of wedging silently.

stories.title: Kiosk watchdog -- auto-restart eclipse-dashboard when the renderer wedges
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #2] add a watchdog that detects a wedged renderer (e.g. AllocateRingBuffer error-rate spike, or a CPU-pegged chromium with no state-file-driven repaint) and restarts eclipse-dashboard to restore a fresh GPU context (the proven live mitigation)

conservative trigger: restart only on a genuine wedge, never flap under normal operation; log every restart so recurring wedges stay visible (defense-in-depth behind US-522, must not mask a still-present freeze class)
test proves the watchdog triggers a restart on a simulated wedge and no-ops under healthy operation; ruff clean in-loop

validationCriteria.action: simulate/observe a renderer wedge on the Pi
validationCriteria.outcome: eclipse-dashboard is auto-restarted and the display recovers with no human intervention; the restart is logged

conditionalOutcomes: watchdog is defense-in-depth, NOT the primary fix (US-522). It must surface recurring wedges, not silence them.
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the kiosk to recover itself if the renderer ever wedges, so the display never stays silently frozen (honest-instrument).

verify post-boot CmaTotal reflects the raise (was 65536 kB)

stories.title: Splash render fix -- boot splash visibility + shutdown-splash 401 route
acceptance: [Atlas READ 2026-08-02] the 401 on bare routes /boot /shutdown is BY-DESIGN: states_http_server routes index / (token-injected, 200), static assets by extension incl *.html (200), everything else -> token-gated state-file lookup -> 401 (:232-234). Bare /boot / /shutdown match no servable-page bucket. The token gate is CORRECT (US-393 SSOT) -- US-501's _injectHtml is EXONERATED (index path serves 200)

FIRST establish what actually requests /boot / /shutdown before assuming the 401 is even on the render path. Likely I-042 causes: (a) URL/route-contract mismatch -- a splash launcher requests a bare route the server serves only at / or *.html; (b) boot-splash visibility timing -- US-494 HEALTHY_YIELD self-close flashes sub-second before it can be seen
boot splash: if too-fast, add a minimum-visible-duration floor so the brand splash is actually seen; hand off to the dashboard after
shutdown splash: ensure the grace/launcher loads a SERVED route (/ or *.html with token injection), not a bare 401 route, so the reverse splash renders on a real shutdown

if the fix adds explicit served splash routes for /boot / /shutdown, they MUST serve the splash HTML with same-origin token injection (like the index path _serveIndex/_injectHtml) -- KEEP the gate, never bypass or weaken _tokenOk (that re-opens TD-067 and is an Atlas BLOCK)
honest-instrument: splash reflects real boot/shutdown state; test proves the routes the splash launcher requests return 200 with the token; ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: reboot the Pi and observe the boot splash; then trigger a shutdown and observe the shutdown splash
validationCriteria.outcome: boot splash is visibly shown then hands off to the dashboard; shutdown reverse splash renders on shutdown

conditionalOutcomes: [Atlas condition -- not a block unless violated] any design that weakens _tokenOk on any route, or makes bare routes public, is an Atlas BLOCK (TD-067 destructive-token-gate). Flag before implementing
stories.goal: As the operator, I want to see the boot and shutdown splash, so the Pi shows an honest brand + boot/shutdown state instead of a blank hand-off.

stories.title: US-504a production drain-event writer (battery_health_log grows again)
acceptance: [CARRIED from Sprint 69 / BL-028] build the PRODUCTION drain-event writer. No production caller in src/ has written battery_health_log since US-216 auto-open was retired (US-442/TD-058). BatteryHealthRecorder.startDrainEvent/endDrainEvent already write the columns correctly -- wire a production caller

[SEAM] PowerMonitor.onTransition is the registration point; PowerMonitor already receives GPIO6 truth via the US-502 _PowerSourceUiBridge sink. Read the UPS LATE-BOUND at transition time, not captured at construction (US-501/502/503 boot-order trap)

on a real AC->BATTERY transition open a drain row with a REAL start_vcell_v + start_soc_pct from the MAX17048; on BATTERY->AC or cutoff shutdown close it with real end_vcell_v/end_soc_pct + runtime_seconds. Honest-instrument: an unreadable gauge writes NULL, never a guessed number (reuse readCalibratedRegisterSocPct + its cold-start window)

[ORPHAN POLICY -- Atlas RULING 2026-08-02: Option C CONFIRMED] open-at-loss + close-at-restore-or-shutdown, ShutdownSequencer close PRIMARY + boot reaper crash BACKSTOP. Spool's depth gate (end_vcell_v <= [EXACT:3.50] V + [EXACT:60] s floor) disqualifies option B (a memory-held row lost to a hard crash drops the run-to-cutoff drain the verdict needs) and demotes the reaper to hygiene-only

[LOAD-BEARING INVARIANT -- code-confirmed battery_health.py:84-85,100,118-120] endDrainEvent computes runtime_seconds from the start/end timestamp delta, so the boot reaper MUST NOT call endDrainEvent (across a reboot it would manufacture a multi-hour runtime). The reaper uses its OWN UPDATE stamping ONLY end_timestamp, leaving BOTH runtime_seconds NULL AND end_vcell_v NULL (honest-NA: an interrupted drain's depth is unknown, never fabricated -- a fabricated end_vcell_v <= 3.50 under the depth gate would be a worse trap than the runtime one; NULL on either field also fails the depth gate = double-safe). Reaper targets ONLY still-open rows (WHERE end_timestamp IS NULL), respecting first-close-wins (battery_health.py:123-125), never clobbering a legit ShutdownSequencer close
[Rule-10 -- shutdown path is load-bearing] update specs/architecture.md battery-health / drain-recorder + shutdown section IN-SPRINT (DoD, not a follow-up)

test proves: a production AC<->battery transition writes real vcell/soc; a cutoff-shutdown drain is closed by the ShutdownSequencer ON the shutdown path (not just a warm unit test); a reaped orphan is EXCLUDED by the depth-gate verdict (runtime_seconds NULL + end_vcell_v NULL -> not counted); ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi force an AC->battery->AC transition (or bench harness) and query battery_health_log
validationCriteria.outcome: a new row with real start/end vcell + soc + runtime_seconds; an interrupted drain leaves an orphan with runtime_seconds NULL, never a fabricated runtime

conditionalOutcomes: Atlas CONFIRMED Option C + the reaper-NULL invariant 2026-08-02 (offices/pm/inbox/2026-08-02-from-atlas-v0.29.25-prd-review.md). Depth-gate qualifying values ride US-527 (Spool [EXACT]). Live fold = the BL-025 engine-on drive
stories.goal: As the operator, I want battery_health_log to gain real rows from actual drains, so the Health verdict can leave 'unknown' honestly.

[EXACT] values are load-bearing -- flag Spool before any drift (review-stories gate)
